punchline: Seneca scolded his bailiff about the plane trees, then remembered he had planted them himself.
thirty_sec: In Letter 12 Seneca visits his old country house, sees crumbling walls, leafless plane trees and the old slave Felicio at the door, and realises he has aged; he urges us to cherish old age and to close each day as if it were the last.
question: Which task or conversation, finished before bed tonight, would make it easier to say you lived today?
key_contrast: Pacuvius staged his funeral dinner daily from a debased motive; Seneca asks for the same ritual from a good one.
